## 1. The question, frozen

The opening does not pose a question; it says the Time Traveller "was expounding a recondite matter." That matter is his case that **Time is a fourth dimension of Space, and therefore a machine can travel in Time.** So I freeze that as central: *What makes travelling in Time possible?*, over bodies and machines, asked forward (from causes). Two things get conflated and must be kept apart: the argument answers the forward question, while the vanishing model answers a backward one — *what can we tell from what we saw?* A good backward answer is not a good forward one (in-depth, §6).

## 2. The explanation in parts (owner's words)

- **P1** "Any real body must have extension in four directions … Length, Breadth, Thickness, and — Duration" (the *instantaneous cube* argument).
- **P2** "Time is only a kind of Space" / "no difference … except that our consciousness moves along it."
- **P3** the weather record: "the mercury … traced such a line … along the Time-Dimension."
- **P4** "a natural infirmity of the flesh … we incline to overlook this fact."
- **P5** the gravity analogy: "Gravitation limits us there … before the balloons … man had no freedom of vertical movement."
- **P6** "Our mental existences … are passing along the Time-Dimension with a uniform velocity."
- **P7** "presentation below the threshold … diluted presentation"; the machine gone at "one-fiftieth or one-hundredth" visibility.
- **P8** the demonstration: the model vanishes; "I am absolutely certain there was no trickery."

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Because |
|---|---|---|
| P1 duration | **Held** — by the instantaneous-cube job | Remove Duration and a real cube "does not last"; that job holds it. But it holds *bodies last*, not *you can move along Time* — for the central question it is **idle**. |
| P2 "Time is only a kind of Space" | **Borrowed** — rests on four-dimensional geometry (Newcomb, "our mathematicians"), untested here | Swap "Space" for a dimension you cannot move in and the line still stands. |
| P3 barometer line | **Loose** — any graph would do | A plotted line is a *reading*; watch the part and it moves when only the record moves. It answers "what can we tell." |
| P4 "infirmity of the flesh" | **Loose** | Swap the reason we overlook it (habit, training) — the argument is unchanged. |
| P5 gravity analogy | **Held if** — by the doubtful job "our immobility in Time is no bar to a dimension" | Gravity limits a *range*; our immobility in Time is total. The concession "there are balloons" undercuts the analogy it was built to save. |
| P6 "mental existences" drifting along Time | **Loose** | If we already move along Time, the machine's job shrinks; the part could be dropped. |
| P7 "diluted presentation" | **Borrowed** — a "simple point in psychology," untested here | Also a near-**catch-all**: it absorbs any failure. Its only gauge is faint (the "breath of wind," the flame jumping, the candle blown out) — yet the machine vanished wholly, not faintly. |
| P8 the model vanishes | **Two routes** — time travel *or* a conjuring trick | Nothing on the change list tells the two apart; the Medical Man names the rival ("like that ghost you showed us last Christmas"). |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

- **Flip.** Had the model stayed on the table, "diluted presentation" covers that too (it hadn't reached the threshold). An answer that fits both outcomes is held by neither (§5).
- **Direction.** The story runs backward from the result: it vanished, *so* it went through Time. Poke the effect (make it vanish by a trick) and the cause doesn't move. Fine for "what can we tell," not for "what produces."
- **Answer hidden in the starting points.** "Time is only a kind of Space" carries the motion inside the word "dimension." The conclusion — *you can move in Time* — is already sitting in the premise, as "dimension of Space." (§5, §6).
- **Where the jobs came from.** J1 "why is Time regarded as different?" — *given* (Medical Man). J2 "why can't we move in Time?" — *given* (Psychologist). J3 "why can't we see it?" — *added* by the Psychologist to rescue the vanishing. J4 past-vs-future — *added*. P7 is held only by an added job, so it is held *only if* that job is real.
- **Pull.** P5 ("you cannot move at all in Time") pulls against P6 ("we are always getting away from the present moment"). One says Time is a wall, the other says it is a drift. Each passes alone; at the joint they fight.
- **Patch.** The one live challenge (conjuring) is not answered — it is met with the conditions and "I don't want to be told I'm a quack." A patch narrowing the claim, not a test.
- **Change list.** It has one fixed outcome (vanished) and one speed parameter. It leaves out: a machine that *returns*; a witness effect left mid-journey; any case where travel should be *blocked*. Nothing on it could have come out otherwise.
- **Rival.** "It was a trick" answers every change the text runs, identically. As put, the two are the same explanation at this level.

**Where parts came from.** P2, P7 *borrowed*; P5 *fitted* to the objection it meets; P1 *built* (worked from the cube) but for a side point; P4, P8 *asserted*.

## 5. What would make it hardest to vary

1. **Unfix the outcome.** Press the reverse lever and have the model come *back*, carrying something from its journey. Now there is a change to the world the claim covers.
2. **Separate the rival.** Name one change that a conjuring trick and a time journey answer differently, and run it (a returning machine; a witness impression mid-voyage).

## 6. What this does not show

Loose is not false. The argument is loose; that does not show time travel is impossible. This tool finds which bolts are tight, not whether the machine is true.

## 7. One next step

Make the machine *return* — a single change that turns the one fixed outcome into a test, and that a conjuring trick could not match.
